extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners, patent attorneys, and applicants (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining identicalness of inventions, applying Article 29 (enlarged novelty/disclosure exceptions) and Article 36 (first-to-file) of the Korean Patent Act, and detailed examination procedures for conflicting and international applications. Covers reference-date rules, substantial identicalness categories, and examiner procedures for conflicting applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'laid open to public inspection' for international applications (pre/post Jan 1, 2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications filed on or before Dec 31, 2014 and for those filed on or after Jan 1, 2015, specifies what 'laid open to public inspection' and 'a specification or drawings originally attached to a patent application' refer to when applying Article 29(3)-(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an application is filed on and before Dec 31, 2014, reference to a 'specification or drawings originally attached' refers to the translation of the specification, claims or drawings of the international application submitted at filing. For applications filed on and after Jan 1, 2015, 'laid open' includes international publication under Article 21 of the PCT and 'specification or drawings originally attached' refers to description, claims or drawings submitted until the date of filing the international application. Additionally, if an international application is deemed withdrawn because a Korean translation of the description and claims was not submitted within the period under Article 214(4), it cannot be relied upon under Article 29(3) and (4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Article 29 to international applications claiming domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: When Article 29(3)-(6) is applied to an international patent application claiming domestic priority, inventions disclosed both in the international application's specification/claims/drawings and in its translation are relevant; an invention disclosed in the specification or drawings of a prior-filed domestic application on which priority is claimed shall be deemed laid open to public inspection when the international application is published under PCT Article 21 or published for registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a later-filed application is identical to the invention disclosed in the prior-filed application's specification/claims/drawings submitted at the prior application's international filing date, the later application may be rejected based on that prior-filed disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of enlarged novelty for international applications under Article 29(5)-(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: When another application is an international application under Article 29 paragraphs 5 and 6, the extent of enlarged novelty applied is the invention(s) disclosed both in the specification, claims or drawings of the international application submitted at its international filing date and in its translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if another application claims domestic priority from a prior-filed international application and the invention of the present application is identical to that disclosed in the prior-filed application's specification/claims/drawings submitted at the prior-filed application's international filing date, the present application may be rejected over that prior-filed disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of Determination of Identicalness (overview/procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of whether Article 29(3) and (4) apply refers to whether a claimed invention is identical to an invention specified in the description or drawings in another application at its filing (a 'prior art reference').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (1) Determine the claimed invention of the present application (method same as determining novelty). (2) Determine the disclosure of the prior art reference by the description of the specification of the other application; inherent disclosure obvious in light of common general knowledge may be considered. (3) Compare claimed invention with the prior art reference to find identicalness and differences (do not compare with a combination of more than two prior art references). (4) If no difference is found between the subject matters defining the claimed invention and the prior art reference, they are identical; identicalness includes substantial identicalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial method for determining identicalness (principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identicalness of invention is related to novelty, inventive step, disclosure exception, enlarged concept of novelty, protection of lawful holder, first-to-file, succession, divisional and converted applications, and priority claims; the same criteria apply across these cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination relies on comparison of subject matter defining the claimed invention and the prior art reference. If differences exist, inventions are not identical; if no difference or complete/substantial identicalness exists, they are identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'substantially identical' inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Substantially identical' refers to cases where differences are merely non-substantial (secondary matters) that do not concern the technical ideas of the inventions — e.g., simple differences in expression, recognition of effects, purposes or use, simple change in configuration, or simple differences in usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination for enlarged concept of novelty under Article 29(3) should be based on identicalness of technical configuration and the effects of the inventions. Even if technical configurations differ but differences are only in detailed means for solving technical issues (mere addition/deletion/change of prior arts) that do not create new effects, the inventions are deemed substantially identical (Supreme Court Case No. 2006 Hu 1452, Mar 13, 2008).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference in expression (treated as non-substantial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in expression refer to cases where expressions used in patent claims differ but contents are substantially the same; such differences are treated as 'difference in expressions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The method of desalination of sea water' vs 'the method of concentration of sea water' by separating water through insertion of an undissolved refrigerant — different wording but same content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference in recognition of effects (treated as non-substantial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in recognition of effects occur where recognition of an invention's effects differs even though the effects are identical due to identical configurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Prior-filed application discloses a conductor covered with polyethylene and states greater electric insulation; later-filed application discloses better high frequency properties — different recognition of effects though configuration identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference in purposes (treated as non-substantial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in purposes refer to subjective purposes of the inventions differing even though the configurations are the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If configurations are identical and differences are only in expressed purposes, this is a non-substantial difference for identicalness assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in configurations (mere changes treated as non-substantial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in configuration refer to cases where configuration is changed into another invention by mere substitution, addition, deletion or other simple alterations that a person skilled in the art could easily make and that do not lead to significant changes in purposes and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such changes include 'mere change of means', 'mere addition or deletion of means', 'mere change of material or substitution of equivalents', 'mere change of equal means', 'mere limitation or change of figures, numbers or sequence', and 'mere limitation or change of figures'. If these changes do not materially affect purposes/effects, they are non-substantial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere change of means (subcategory of configuration change)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere change of means occurs when the configuration is changed (becoming another invention) but the change does not lead to significant differences in the purposes and effects of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A manufacturing process of clarifying pure fruit juice by using bentonite and then vacuum freeze drying the juice into powdered fruit juice' vs '...by using diatomite then vacuum freeze drying' — change of clarifying agent but same overall effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere addition or deletion of means (subcategory of configuration change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere addition or deletion of means refers to a configuration change by addition or deletion that does not lead to significant differences in purposes and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Two processes for producing P-nitrotoluene with minor additive steps; if changes do not materially alter purpose/effect they are mere addition/deletion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere change of material or substitution of equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to replacing materials or articles with comparable or functionally identical alternatives that do not lead to significant differences in purposes and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A foundation pile with blades attached on the concrete shack' vs 'a foundation pile with blades on the shack pile' — substitution/variation in material/placement that preserves function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere change of equal means
rubrics_metrics.description: Change to means having comparability or the same function such that no significant differences in purposes/effects arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat substitution by equivalent functional means as non-substantial for identicalness assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere limitation or change of figures, numbers or sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes that limit or alter figures, numbers or sequence in ways a skilled person would commonly apply, without producing significant differences in purposes/effects, are non-substantial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes mere limitation or change of figures; such numerical/sequence adjustments are not substantive differences when effect/purpose remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences in mere use
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in use where two inventions with different configurations are distinguished only by their uses, and such differences can be derived from other configurations, are treated as mere use differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A plasticizer of PVC comprising compound B' vs 'A ultraviolet light absorber of PVC comprising compound B' (same composition but different described use). Another example: spraying chemical A to repel hares vs deer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of use limitation (mere limitation of uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases where the difference is whether uses are limited; such use-limitation differences derived from other configurations are mere use limitations and non-substantial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A net comprising threads with flat cross sections' vs 'A fish net comprising threads with flat cross sections' — difference only in stated use (fish) and thus non-substantial.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-File entitlement rules (Article 36 overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 36: where at least two patent applications for an identical invention are filed on different dates, only the applicant of the earliest filing date is entitled to a patent; if filed on the same date, only the person agreed upon by all applicants may obtain a patent; provisions extend mutatis mutandis when patent and utility model applications overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (4) lists cases where an application shall be deemed never filed (abandoned, invalidated, withdrawn, or final rejection), with provisos. Paragraph (5) treats applications filed by persons who are not inventors or successors as deemed never filed for purposes of Article 36 paragraphs (1)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications lacking status as prior-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application or utility model registration application that is invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or where a decision/trial decision to reject has become final and conclusive does not hold status as a prior-filed application. Also, an application filed by a person who is neither an inventor nor successor does not hold prior-filed status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: a final and conclusive rejection result may still allow prior-filed status in cases covered by latter sentence of Article 36(2) (applies to applications filed after Mar 3, 2006) — aimed to prevent applicants re-filing to evade first-to-file rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date rules for determining earliest-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date used to determine earliest filing is recognized as: (i) actual filing date for applications without priority; (ii) filing date of the application which is the basis of the priority claim for treaty priority claims (for multiple priority claims, earliest filing date among each invention); (iii) filing date of the application serving as basis for domestic priority (similar multiple-priority rule); (iv) filing date of the original application for divisional and converted applications; (v) for applications filed by lawful holder of a right (misappropriation), the reference date is the filing date of the misappropriated application and the misappropriated application is deemed never filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply for international applications: for those filed on/before Dec 31, 2014 the reference date is the filing date in which invention is disclosed in the translation; for those filed on/after Jan 1, 2015 the reference date is the date of filing the international application on invention disclosed in the specification or drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination approach when conflicting applications filed on different dates
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than two applications for the same invention are filed on different dates, the earliest filer is entitled; examiners must apply Article 29(3)-(4) or Article 36 depending on applicant/inventor identity and publication status of prior-filed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant and inventor are not the same and the prior-filed application is laid open/registered, Article 29(3)-(4) primarily apply to later-filed applications; proviso on enlarged novelty can be flexibly applied within specification/drawings if prior-filed is already laid open even before claims confirmed. If a prior-filed application is not laid open, examination on the later application is postponed until prior-filed is laid open or registered. If applicant of later-filed is same as prior or inventors are same, Article 36 applies and examiner should make rejection decision after claims in prior-filed are confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination approach when conflicting applications filed on same date
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than two applications for the same invention are filed on the same date, only the person agreed upon by all applicants may obtain a patent; if no agreement is reached, none obtains a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agreement is reached, submit report of change of right relation in specified Enforcement Rules form and carry out subsequent proceedings (withdrawal of conflicting applications etc.). An applicant receiving a request for consultation can address grounds for rejection by amending or deleting conflicting invention claims without consultation. The same rules apply when patent and utility model applications are filed on same date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation on conflicting applications (examiner checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: When conflicting applications are found, the examiner should check whether the patent applicant is identical, and whether conflicting applications are invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or have a final decision to reject, in which case they do not hold prior-filed status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflicting application does not hold prior-filed status, the examiner shall consider that the conflicting application has never been filed. Note: conflicting applications where applicant/inventor differ are rare; typical cases arise from incorrect claim amendments when filing divisionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when the applicant of conflicting application is different
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant of a conflicting application is different, the examiner must follow special procedures: notify parties, request consultation, and manage examination/postponement as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflicting application is laid open and requested for examination, the examiner shall request consultation under the name of the Commissioner within designated period and notify grounds for rejection under Article 36(2) or (3) (grounds may be in a separate notice). If, after consultation, the applicant remedies the ground (reports result and takes measures), the examiner shall grant the patent; otherwise, reject. If the conflicting application is yet to be laid open or requested for examination, postpone examination of the present application until the conflicting application is requested for examination, withdrawn or abandoned. When a conflicting application is granted and applicants are different, notify the present applicant of the conflicting relation through the On-nara System and indicate the conflicting relation in the ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when the applicant of conflicting application is identical
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicants are identical across conflicting applications, the examiner applies Article 36 procedures: issue notice of rejection if conflicting application is granted or final rejection arises; if conflicting application not yet granted, notify other grounds for rejection without reviewing Article 36(2) or (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a notified ground for rejection has been remedied and the reexamination shows the conflicting application's consequence (grant/rejection) yet undecided, and no other ground remains, a patent may be granted to the present application. If a patent is granted to the conflicting application, the present application may be rejected accordingly. Examiner must consider remedial amendments and the timing of decisions on conflicting applications.
